meta.guideline: CHEERS 2022 - Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022
meta.citation: Husereau D, Drummond M, Augustovski F, et al., on behalf of the CHEERS 2022 ISPOR Good Research Practices Task Force. Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) Statement: Updated Reporting Guidance for Health Economic Evaluations. Value Health. 2022;25(1):3-9.
meta.licence: CHEERS 2022 checklist (Table 1) (c) 2022 ISPOR / the authors, from Husereau et al., Value Health 2022;25(1):3-9, doi:10.1016/j.jval.2021.11.1351, published Open Access under CC BY 4.0. Guidance text reproduced verbatim with no changes; the Statement's own slips (items 24, 25, 27, 28) are preserved deliberately.
meta.locator_note: P<n>/J<n> = PDF page / printed journal page of the Statement (P1 = J3). Table 1 items 1-23 are on P3/J5; items 24-28 on P4/J6. App. A = Appendix A (GRIPP2 short form, mmc1.docx); App. B = Appendix B (Delphi protocol, mmc2.docx).
meta.scope_sentence: Reporting completeness only, not the quality of the study's conduct or the appropriateness of its methods (CHEERS 2022: use 'should be limited to assessing the quality of reporting of a study rather than the quality of its conduct', P4/J6; the Statement 'is not intended as a scoring tool or a tool to assess the appropriateness of methods', P2/J4).
meta.ee_note: CHEERS asks users to 'first consult the Explanation and Elaboration report to ensure the appropriate interpretation of each item description' (P4/J6). That report was not available to this skill; items are judged against the Table 1 guidance text only.
meta.tally_note: Tally (arithmetic only; CHEERS 2022 has 'no validated scoring system' and scoring 'is strongly discouraged', P4/J6)
meta.clause_note: clauses are the skill's decomposition of each item's guidance into verbatim fragments, used to decide Addressed vs Partially addressed; they are not CHEERS sub-items.

cross_checks.check: Uncertainty methods described in 20 have their effect on findings reported in 24 (and vice versa).
If discounting is applied or the horizon choice could change results, 24 reports the effect of the discount rate and time horizon ('if applicable').
Engagement described in 21 is followed by its effect in 25; an explicit no-engagement statement makes both Not applicable; silence on both makes both Missing.
cross_checks.basis: Table 1 topics 'Approach to engagement' / 'Effect of engagement'; App. A (R23, R33)

cross_checks.check: The study type is used consistently: if modelling is used, 16 and 22 apply and 17's validation clause applies; if not, 16 and 22 are Not applicable (R14).
